source_review.notes: Checked publisher or primary records for CLRS, McIlroy's quicksort adversary, Bentley/McIlroy sort engineering, USENIX algorithmic-complexity attacks, QuickCheck, coverage-guided property testing, and delta debugging. Checked the current OWASP ReDoS reference while keeping engine behavior implementation-scoped.

evidence: Defined legal input sets, implementation cost, worst-case maximum, generator parameters/seed, predicate, and budgets.
Checked size, comparisons, time, bytes, amplification, probability, and resource-unit language.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every adversarial claim is bound to a target and adversary model.

evidence: Recomputed length-eight sorted, reversed, and all-equal comparison counts as 28 and balanced-order cost as 13.
Recomputed the length-ten witness as 45 comparisons and independently checked 75 family cases.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts measure the declared comparison model rather than machine time.

evidence: Checked the implication from one witness C_A(x)=c to W_A(n)>=c and the absence of a converse upper-bound claim.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The recurrence premises specify first-pivot two-way partitioning.

evidence: Reviewed empty, singleton, equal, ordered, reversed, cutoff-neighbor, memory-spill, collision, backtracking, numeric, cache, concurrency, and I/O pathologies.
Reviewed invalid preconditions, leaked/random seeds, adaptive feedback, uncontrolled escalation, shrink mechanism drift, machine overfit, and signature-specific defenses.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Typical, boundary, pathology, malicious, and invalid panels remain distinct.

evidence: Checked legality, semantic oracle, independent size/budget, declared knowledge, resource isolation, panel separation, and shrink-predicate invariants.
Exhaustively checked sorting correctness and comparison bounds for all 720 permutations of six distinct values.
invariant_checking.notes: Risky experiments remain local, bounded, nonprivileged, and non-production.

evidence: Reviewed the quicksort chain recurrence for sorted and all-equal inputs under the exact partition rule.
Reviewed counterexample and shrink-integrity logic, including why unsuccessful search proves no upper bound.
proof_review.notes: Testing evidence is not promoted to exhaustive or asymptotic proof.

evidence: Audited boundary, pathological, adversarial, adaptive, oblivious, invalid, witness, family, lower bound, upper bound, exhaustive, and locally minimal language.
Separated algorithm theorem, implementation witness, machine-specific cost, security threat model, and prevalence estimate.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No negative search result is called proof of safety.

evidence: The CPython 3.14.4 snippet produced exact comparison counts and sorted outputs on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
Independent checks covered 75 pathology-family fixtures and all 720 size-six permutations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes only the declared reference implementation and fixtures, not production sorting behavior.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed adversary models, pathology taxonomy, proof-derived inputs, threshold surfaces, generation/search, adaptive feedback, isolation, oracles, shrinking, defenses, panels, and conservative negative results.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed local disposable workers, resource ceilings, escalation stops, preserved seeds/inputs, exact target/build identity, oracle independence, privacy, no external targeting, rerunnable reduction, and defense regression.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter unifies theoretical witnesses with operational and security stress testing, supplies an executable case, ten distinct examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, pedagogical, and safety review only; no external academic, security, red-team, runtime, operating-system, hardware, service-owner, or production review is claimed. Conclusions remain conditional on target implementation, legal-input contract, cost model, adversary knowledge/control/adaptation, random state, generator and victim budgets, oracle, isolation, platform, toolchain, and observed search scope.
